support-alex: Heads-up — customer `acme-recs` is seeing inconsistent embedding lengths from /v1/embeddings. Expected 1536 but ~1-2% responses are 1024. No 500s, just wrong dims. Happening during peak windows where we have a lot of high-priority traffic. Escalating.

support-alex: Minimal repro and quick logs below. They send batched requests with a priority_tag header and small inputs. Request IDs for examples: rq_acme_01, rq_acme_02. Tracer: trace-01-xy.

support-alex: repro (curl):
```bash
curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"text-embedding-3-large","input":["hi","hello","search term"],"priority_tag":"acme-urgent"}' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings
```

support-alex: observed payload/response from rq_acme_01:
```
[INFO] batch_id=bnr-42 composition=[{shard:gpu-7,model:text-embedding-3-large,dim:1536,reqs:12},{shard:gpu-3,model:text-embedding-3-small,dim:1024,reqs:3}]
[WARN] response_stream merged for batch bnr-42; client_rq=rq_acme_01 -> returned vec_len=1024
```

eng-runtime-sam: thanks for the clear repro. My hunch: dynamic batch merging + priority preemption is letting batches that should be homogenous get merged across model variants (or different quant profiles). That would explain mixed dims. Can you attach the full batch composition log and the per-request model_hint headers? Also please paste the raw base64 length header if available.

support-alex: attaching snippets in ticket but pasted relevant lines above. model_hint header present: `model=text-embedding-3-large` on all client reqs. We do see the scheduler creating a batch that contains a second group with `text-embedding-3-small`. Not sure why that small variant got in — possibly fallback variant selected by shard due to capacity.

eng-ml-jia: I reproduced locally by forcing a preemptive slot reassign. The scheduler can merge windows when idle but our invariants assume variant homogeneity. Two plausible causes: 1) routing fallback that maps to a compatible variant without updating the per-request dim metadata before merging, or 2) KV-cache/serialization bug where output buffer from one executor gets reused for another.

eng-ml-jia: quick mitigation suggestions:
- disable cross-variant coalescing in the batcher (config: batching.allow_variant_merge=false)
- lower max_batch_size for the affected route to reduce merge events (route config override)
- return a 500 on homogeneity mismatch so client can retry (safer than returning wrong-dim vector)

eng-sre-maya: I can patch the batcher config to disallow variant merges for the `acme-recs` customer route and push a canary within 30m. I'll also add an assertion to the batch commit that validates `expected_dim == emitted_dim` and logs the first mismatch. That will make repros much easier.

customer-ops-linda: Reached out to customer with two asks: (1) try without priority_tag (they're hesitant), (2) we can set route override to force no-merge. They prefer a server-side fix.

eng-runtime-sam: For a fast server-side fix, I'll add a guard so the merger checks per-request model_hint + variant_id before merging; if mismatch, it forces split. That should be low-risk and reversible. I'll also add an emergency handler that if a mismatch is detected post-hoc, we drop the response and mark the request for retry rather than returning a wrong-sized vector. Planning a canary deploy.

deploy-bot: deploy request: batcher-safety-guard v0.1 -> canary (3/20 nodes) started by eng-runtime-sam.

eng-ml-jia: FYI I ran a synthetic load that mixes priority and non-priority traffic and reproduced the 1024/1536 split in ~40 runs. With variant-merge disabled the issue stops. Patch PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/batcher/pull/342 (tests + sim).

support-alex: Added notes to escalation #4567 and notified customer. Will monitor the canary. Thanks team. :thumbsup:
